name: Down to Nothing
label: Revelation
lede: Two kids who'd been friends since age five turned a Grace Street all-ages room into a straight edge crew, wrote love songs to the James River, and kept the band going while the singer played bass in Terror almost three hundred days a year.

eras.title: The Guerrilla Crew on Grace Street
eras.text: Down to Nothing came out of a teenage straight edge crew in Richmond, Virginia, a city whose early-2000s shows could get violent. They played Twisters on Grace Street, cut records for Thorp, and learned the road by setting off fireworks in Sheffield.

years.h: Down to Nothing's first show at Twisters, 929 Grace Street
years.p: High-schoolers David Wood and Daniel Spector, friends since age five, start the band with guitarist Alan Long. The first show, possibly still under the name Detonation, is at Twisters with Shut Down and From Earth to Ashes.
years.xp:
Wood told Dying Scene he'd started experimenting with drugs at about twelve, before hardcore pulled him to straight edge. The band grew out of the Guerrilla Crew, a straight edge collective of Richmond teenagers.

Twisters later became Strange Matter. Spector and guitarist Ryan "Groater" Groat split the riff-writing in the early years.

years.h: Down to Nothing's first 7" on Dead By 23
years.p: Down to Nothing's demo comes out on Dead By 23 Records. David Wood is eighteen.

years.h: Save It for the Birds · Thorp Records
years.p: Down to Nothing's first full-length, on Thorp Records.

years.h: Florida bassist Jared Carman joins Down to Nothing
years.p: Down to Nothing meet Jared Carman's band in Daytona and recruit him on bass for their 2005 tour. Carman later also plays in [[Trapped Under Ice|94c44a31-3f7b-4c5d-aa54-2bf47eeac5d5]].
Eleven tracks in under 21 minutes, opening on Go Ahead wit Yo' Fake Ass and closing on I'm So Lucky.
play: Go Ahead wit Yo' Fake Ass

years.h: Down to Nothing's Guy Fawkes night in Sheffield
years.p: On Down to Nothing's first UK tour, with On Thin Ice, the band play Sheffield on Guy Fawkes Day. David Wood says they bought heaps of fireworks and ran amok all night.

eras.title: Richmond on Revelation
eras.text: Revelation, home of Judge and Gorilla Biscuits, took on the Richmond band. Three records in three years followed, one with a Have Heart guest, and then the singer got a job offer from Terror.

years.h: Higher Learning 7", Down to Nothing's first for Revelation
years.p: Revelation REV 140: 104 purple, 328 orange and 614 yellow on the first pressing.
Produced by Jim Siegel. Up River features Patrick Flynn of [[Have Heart|e519e012-e1a3-4592-b3f6-5a16227ab654]], the band whose reunion Down to Nothing would play twelve years later.
Revelation presses 330 white and 330 red. Daniel Spector writes new material on that year's European tour.

q: Terror is professional. DTN is goofy chaos vacation.
years.h: David Wood joins Terror on bass
years.p: Down to Nothing's singer becomes the bassist for [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]]. He calls Terror serious and professional, and Down to Nothing goofy chaos vacation.

eras.title: Terror is the job
eras.text: With David Wood on the road with Terror, Down to Nothing went quiet for long stretches. They were still under contract to Revelation, but new music came out on Reaper.

years.h: Down to Nothing's All My Sons 7" on Reaper
years.p: Down to Nothing hadn't played since January 2010 when David Wood told Dying Scene Terror was his job, on the road almost 300 days a year. All My Sons gets a July 4 release show and a Sound and Fury set.

years.h: Live at Sound and Fury, July 24, 2010
yt: Live at Sound and Fury, July 24, 2010

eras.title: Love letters to the James River
eras.text: Five years after Unbreakable, Down to Nothing made a record about Richmond itself: its river, its park, its all-ages rooms. By then the drummer was an emergency medicine resident, and fans were making pilgrimages.

years.p: Revelation REV 152: 520 yellow, 526 white and 550 black.

years.big: Fans drove from Florida to see Belle Isle
q: Every band from out of town felt like they had a home in Richmond.
years.h: Life on the James, Down to Nothing's ode to Richmond · REV 153
years.p: Daniel Spector writes all the music, now while working as an emergency medicine resident at VCU. The songs name Richmond spots, and fans drive up from Florida to see Shafer Court and Belle Isle.
years.xp:
RVA Mag credited the band with helping turn Richmond's early-2000s shows, which could be violent, into a more welcoming scene, following [[Avail|d67ff511-57b8-4d02-94d3-6c6a331c2ae4]] and [[Strike Anywhere|ac82cb46-f2b2-4f99-9cfa-d0c322a4ba16]]. Early shows at Twisters gave way to the Kingdom and Alley Katz.

David Wood calls it his favorite Down to Nothing record.

years.h: David Wood sings for Terror when Scott Vogel slips a disc
years.p: On Terror's 2015 European tour, David Wood steps in on lead vocals after singer [[Scott Vogel|4ab1b4fb-f2fe-458c-a496-0de55c7bf3cb]] slips a disc.
Seventeen songs live, opening with Life on the James. The first pressing runs 1,096 gold and 324 pink. The same year David Wood leaves Terror.

years.h: Last stand: Have Heart's reunion at the Worcester Palladium
years.p: Down to Nothing's final appearance is at [[Have Heart|e519e012-e1a3-4592-b3f6-5a16227ab654]]'s reunion shows at the Worcester Palladium in Massachusetts. After that the band goes inactive.
